title: Paeonia lactiflora

''Paeonia albiflora'' [[Pall.]] }} '''''Paeonia lactiflora''''' ('''Chinese peony''', '''Chinese herbaceous peony''', or '''common garden peony''') is a [[species]] of [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Paeoniaceae, [[native plant|native]] to central and [[East Asia|eastern Asia]] from eastern [[Tibet]] across northern [[China]] to eastern [[Siberia]]. ==Description== It is {{convert|50|-|70|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall and broad, with 9-lobed leaves {{convert|20|-|40|cm|0|abbr=on}} long. The flower buds appear in late spring (May in the Northern Hemisphere). They are large and round, opening into fragrant, cup- or bowl-shaped [[flower]]s {{convert|8|-|16|cm|0|abbr=on}} in diameter, with 5–10 white, pink, or crimson petals and yellow [[stamen]]s.{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}} The plant attracts butterflies.{{Cite web|title=Paeonia lactiflora 'Sarah Bernhardt' - Plant Finder|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=q400|access-date=2021-12-16|website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}} Its habitats include dry open stony slopes, riverbanks and sparse woodland edges.{{Cite web|title=Paeonia lactiflora Chinese Peony, Peony PFAF Plant Database|url=https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Paeonia+lactiflora|access-date=2021-12-16|website=pfaf.org}} == Background == ''Paeonia lactiflora'' was known as the white peony (''P. albiflora'') when first introduced into [[Europe]].{{cite book|last1=Halda|first1=Josef J.|last2=Waddick |first2=James W.|title=The Genus Paeonia|publisher=Timber Press|year=2004|pages=196–205|isbn=978-0-88192-612-5|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mDLASKInbjgC&q=Peony+common+garden&pg=PA196}} It was brought to [[England]] in the mid-18th century, and is the parent of most modern varieties. It has been grown as an ornamental in China since the 7th century. The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''lactiflora'' means "with milk white flowers".{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1845337315 }} In China, ''P. lactiflora'' is likened to "the Minister of Flowers" (花相), while [[Paeonia × suffruticosa|''Paeonia'' × ''suffruticosa'']] is known as "the King of Flowers" (花王).{{Cite web|url=https://www.zdic.net/hans/%E8%8A%B1%E7%9B%B8|title="花相"字的解释 {{!}} 汉典|website=www.zdic.net|language=zh-cn|access-date=2020-01-12}}. They were commonly given at farewells, as a promise to reunite. {{Cite web|url=https://note.com/leal_hare5138/n/n6481370e9ce7}} ==Cultivars== [[File:Paeonia lactiflora 'Sarah Bernhardt.jpg|thumb|cv. 'Sarah Bernhardt']] There are several hundred selected [[cultivar]]s in a range of colours, sizes, and forms. Many have [[double flowers]], with the stamens modified into additional petals.{{cite book|last=Loewer|first=H. Peter|title=Fragrant Gardens|publisher=Houghton Mifflin Gardening|year=1999|pages=[https://archive.org/details/fragrantgardensh00loew/page/48 48]|isbn=978-0-395-88492-8|url=https://archive.org/details/fragrantgardensh00loew|url-access=registration|quote=Peony common garden.}} There are several colors, including white, pink, rose, and near red, with single to fully double forms. They are prolific bloomers, and have become the main source of peonies for the cut flower business. Petals color is dependent on a [[UDP-glucose: Flavonoid 5-O-glucosyltransferase]] expressing anthocyanins such as [[peonidin-3,5-di-O-glucoside]], [[pelargonidin-3,5-di-O-glucoside]], [[cyanidin-3,5-di-O-glucoside]], [[peonidin-3-O-glucoside]], [[cyanidin-3-O-glucoside]], [[peonidin-3-O-glucoside-5-O-arabinoside]], [[cyanidin-3-O-glucoside-5-O-galactoside]] and [[pelargonidin-3-O-glucoside-5-O-galactoside]].Isolation of a UDP-glucose: Flavonoid 5-O-glucosyltransferase gene and expression analysis of anthocyanin biosynthetic genes in herbaceous peony (Paeonia lactiflora Pall.). [[File:Renoir - peonies.jpg!PinterestLarge.jpg|thumb|''Peonies'' 1880 – Pierre-Auguste Renoir]] ''Paeonia lactiflora'' became a popular [[still life]] subject for [[Impressionism|Impressionist]] artists in the late 19th century. *[[Pierre-Auguste Renoir]] featured Peonies in multiple paintings from the 1870s through the 1890s.{{cite web| url=http://www.clarkart.edu/Collection/3121| title='Peonies' Pierre-Auguste Renoir| publisher=clarkart.edu| access-date=2018-04-17| archive-date=2018-04-18|
